name: Transformer foundations
description: A small, inspectable decoder-only transformer. An educational architecture, not a trained checkpoint.
documentation: Start at the architecture overview, then open a block or inspect an edge. Symbolic axes are B (batch), T (current query positions), S (visible key positions), D (hidden width), Hq (query heads), Hkv (KV heads), Dh (features per head), F (FFN width), V (vocabulary) and L (layers). The workbench computes exact dimensions and a real demo BPE trace. Attention probabilities are synthetic examples; no trained model weights are loaded. Optional memory and MTP views illustrate separate architecture extensions. Model definitions, equations, citations, notes, positions and viewports travel together in this versioned JSON document.

tokenizer.description: Deterministic byte-level BPE with a small explicit vocabulary. No pre-tokenization, Unicode normalization or special tokens. See src/model/tokenizer.ts.

sources.title: Attention Is All You Need
sources.note: Scaled dot-product attention, multi-head attention, residual connections and the transformer foundation.

sources.title: tiktoken · educational BPE implementation
sources.note: A reference for byte-level vocabulary-ranked BPE. Our teaching vocabulary and implementation are independent.

sources.title: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models
sources.note: The relationship between query heads, shared KV heads, MHA and MQA.

sources.title: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding
sources.note: Position-dependent rotations of query and key feature pairs.

sources.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention
sources.note: An exact attention kernel with IO-aware tiling; not a different head-sharing scheme.

sources.title: Efficient Memory Management for LLM Serving with PagedAttention
sources.note: Physical KV memory management, separate from logical tensor axes.

sources.title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
sources.note: Reference for sequential MTP and the distinct latent cache representation used by MLA.

sources.title: Better & Faster LLMs via Multi-token Prediction
sources.note: An independent-head multi-token prediction design; distinguish it from sequential MTP.

sources.title: Conditional Memory via Scalable Lookup
sources.note: Engram conditional memory, hashed n-gram retrieval and context-aware fusion.

sources.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
sources.note: Draft / verify / accept-prefix inference. The simulator implements greedy verification, not the paper’s stochastic probability-ratio rule; it makes no speedup claim.

sources.title: Mistral 7B — sliding-window attention and rolling buffer cache
sources.note: Primary account of local causal attention, chunked prefill and a rolling KV buffer. Window conventions are explicit in this workbench.

sources.title: Generating Long Sequences with Sparse Transformers
sources.note: Primary work on structured sparse attention. The fixed absolute anchors plus recent window here are an explicitly illustrative policy, not a reproduction of the paper’s factorized patterns.

graphs.title: Attention, operation by operation.
graphs.subtitle: Follow a query. Inspect every head.
graphs.description: Dense causal attention with configurable MHA, GQA, or MQA sharing. Prefill processes the full prompt; decode processes one new query against a longer cached prefix.

nodes.title: Normalized hidden state
nodes.subtitle: One vector per query position
nodes.description: Input to the layer’s learned query, key and value projections.

nodes.title: Query projection
nodes.subtitle: X · Wq → reshape heads
nodes.description: Multiply by the query weight matrix and reshape to expose the query-head axis.

nodes.title: Key projection
nodes.subtitle: X · Wk → reshape KV heads
nodes.description: Project keys using Hkv heads. Sharing reduces this projection and its persistent cache.

nodes.title: Value projection
nodes.subtitle: X · Wv → reshape KV heads
nodes.description: Values carry the features that attention will average. This architecture applies RoPE to Q and K, not V.

nodes.title: RoPE · queries
nodes.subtitle: Rotate feature pairs by position
nodes.description: Rotate pairs of query features using their absolute token positions. Decode positions continue from the cached prefix.

nodes.title: RoPE · keys
nodes.subtitle: Rotate, then append to cache
nodes.description: Use the same position-dependent rotations for the newly computed keys.

nodes.title: Key cache
nodes.subtitle: Retain positions under the cache policy
nodes.description: Persist rotated keys for this layer. Prior keys are reused; they are not recomputed for every generated token. Full retains the prefix; sliding window retains the latest W positions; sparse retains fixed absolute anchors and a recent window. R counts resident positions; their absolute position IDs remain separate. Cache reads use the prior snapshot; current-call K/V also remain available transiently for all causal queries.

nodes.title: Value cache
nodes.subtitle: Retain positions under the cache policy
nodes.description: Persist values independently from keys, with the same layer, batch, head and sequence indexing. Full retains the prefix; sliding window retains the latest W positions; sparse retains fixed absolute anchors and a recent window. R counts resident positions; their absolute position IDs remain separate. Cache reads use the prior snapshot; current-call K/V also remain available transiently for all causal queries.

nodes.title: Q · Kᵀ
nodes.subtitle: Pairwise query–key dot products
nodes.description: For each query head, select its KV group and contract over Dh. The result has a query-position axis and a key-position axis. U working key slots gather the pre-update retained prefix plus current-call keys. Use their absolute position IDs for masking; an inference kernel need not materialize all scores.
notes: g(h) = floor(h / (Hq/Hkv)) for zero-based, contiguous query-head groups.

nodes.title: Scale + attention mask
nodes.subtitle: Causal visibility · full / window / sparse
nodes.description: Divide by √Dh, then mask every disallowed absolute query/key pair. Full: 0 ≤ k ≤ q. Sliding: max(0,q−W+1) ≤ k ≤ q (W includes the current position). Sparse teaching policy: k ≤ q and (k mod stride = 0 or k > q−W). These are architectural masks; kernels can avoid computing masked pairs. Slot u has absolute position p_u; do not confuse a compact cache index with that position.

nodes.title: Row-wise softmax
nodes.subtitle: Normalize over key positions
nodes.description: For every query position and query head, turn visible scores into non-negative weights that sum to one. Masked positions receive zero weight.
notes: Subtracting each row’s maximum m improves numerical stability.

nodes.title: Attention · V
nodes.subtitle: Weighted sum over visible values
nodes.description: Contract the key-position axis S. Each query head produces Dh features using the V head assigned to its KV group.

nodes.title: Concatenate heads
nodes.subtitle: Transpose + reshape
nodes.description: Move the head axis next to features and flatten Hq×Dh. Concatenation rearranges features; it does not sum heads.

nodes.title: Output projection
nodes.subtitle: Joined heads · Wo
nodes.description: Mix the concatenated head features and return D features to the attention residual branch.
notes: FlashAttention computes the same dense attention with tiled kernels; it need not materialize the full attention matrix. The heatmap here is synthetic teaching data.

graphs.title: The KV cache, in its dimensions.
graphs.subtitle: Layer × batch × KV head × sequence × features.
graphs.description: A logical tensor view of persistent attention state. Inspect a layer and KV head below. Physical allocations may use blocks, strides, quantization, sharding or paging.

nodes.title: New token features
nodes.subtitle: Current layer · current positions
nodes.description: Prefill projects all prompt positions; an ordinary decode step projects one new position.

nodes.title: Project + rotate K
nodes.subtitle: New keys for this layer
nodes.description: Compute this layer’s new keys and apply positional rotations.

nodes.title: Project V
nodes.subtitle: New values for this layer
nodes.description: Compute this layer’s new value features.

nodes.title: Persistent K tensor
nodes.subtitle: Write only the current layer slice
nodes.description: Append keys at the correct sequence positions. The logical all-layer view has axes L, B, Hkv, R, Dh; implementations often store separate tensors per layer. Resident axis R stores retained positions with an absolute-position map. Full keeps all processed keys; sliding keeps the latest W including the current position; sparse keeps fixed-stride absolute anchors plus a recent window. New query-batch keys also remain transiently available before final retention.

nodes.title: Persistent V tensor
nodes.subtitle: A distinct allocation from K
nodes.description: Store values with the same logical indexing as keys. The K/V selector is not an extra attention head. Resident axis R stores retained positions with an absolute-position map. Full keeps all processed keys; sliding keeps the latest W including the current position; sparse keeps fixed-stride absolute anchors plus a recent window. New query-batch keys also remain transiently available before final retention.

nodes.title: Attend to the prefix
nodes.subtitle: Read this layer’s K and V
nodes.description: A query reads visible positions from its assigned KV head. Query heads never share state across decoder layers. Resident axis R stores retained positions with an absolute-position map. Full keeps all processed keys; sliding keeps the latest W including the current position; sparse keeps fixed-stride absolute anchors plus a recent window. New query-batch keys also remain transiently available before final retention.
notes: Resident logical cache bytes = 2 × L × B × Hkv × R × Dh × bytes per scalar. Allocator overhead and quantization metadata are excluded.
PagedAttention changes physical memory management, not the meaning of these logical axes.
MLA requires a different state schema: compressed latent vectors plus positional key state, rather than this full K/V representation.

graphs.title: From hidden states to text.
graphs.subtitle: Normalize. Project. Select. Decode.
graphs.description: The standard next-token output pathway, including the final normalization, vocabulary projection, selection policy and byte decoding.

nodes.title: Final RMSNorm
nodes.subtitle: Normalize the residual stream
nodes.description: Normalize each token vector over its feature dimension before the vocabulary projection. RMSNorm scales by root mean square without subtracting the feature mean.

nodes.title: Vocabulary projection
nodes.subtitle: Hidden state → logits
nodes.description: Project the final hidden state into one logit per vocabulary item. During generation only the last position is needed. The embedding and output weights may be tied, but that is an architecture choice.

nodes.title: Select next token
nodes.subtitle: Temperature · softmax · sampling
nodes.description: Convert last-position logits into a distribution, optionally filter with top-k or top-p, then choose a token. Greedy decoding uses argmax. Temperature must be positive for the softmax formula.
notes: This workbench visualizes structure. It does not run trained weights or generate language.

nodes.description: Map the selected IDs back to bytes and decode the concatenated byte stream. Append the chosen token ID to the model sequence for the next inference step.
notes: Output is detokenization, not re-encoding. Some byte-level tokens are not valid UTF-8 individually.

notes: Inference teaching path. The runnable simulator uses explicitly disclosed tiny, untrained weights.

nodes.title: Draft embedding · depth 2
nodes.subtitle: Embed proposed token t+2
nodes.description: Embed the first MTP prediction to condition the next MTP depth. The proposal chain is sequential, so proposals are not independent.
notes: Inference teaching path. The runnable simulator uses explicitly disclosed tiny, untrained weights.

nodes.title: MTP combine · depth 2
nodes.subtitle: Previous depth + next embedding
nodes.description: The second depth combines the previous MTP hidden state with the next shifted token embedding.
notes: Inference teaching path. The runnable simulator uses explicitly disclosed tiny, untrained weights.

nodes.title: MTP decoder · depth 2
nodes.subtitle: Separate causal decoder block
nodes.description: The second additional decoder block uses its own parameters and state. Two depths are an illustrative configuration, not a claim about every MTP architecture.
notes: Inference teaching path. The runnable simulator uses explicitly disclosed tiny, untrained weights.

nodes.title: MTP prediction · t+3
nodes.subtitle: Third proposed token
nodes.description: The second MTP module proposes the third token using the shared vocabulary projection. All proposals still require main-model verification.
notes: Inference teaching path. The runnable simulator uses explicitly disclosed tiny, untrained weights.

nodes.title: Verify with the main decoder
nodes.subtitle: One causal batch · shifted logits
nodes.description: Run the proposed tokens through the full main decoder using a tentative copy of its KV state. Existing prefix logits verify the first proposal; each batch output verifies the following proposal. The same causal mask and greedy selection rule are used.
notes: Inference teaching path. The runnable simulator uses explicitly disclosed tiny, untrained weights.

nodes.title: Accept the matching prefix
nodes.subtitle: Stop at the first mismatch
nodes.description: In greedy verification, accept proposals only until the first mismatch with the main model. Later proposals cannot be accepted after an earlier mismatch. This is not the probability-ratio acceptance rule used for stochastic speculative sampling.
notes: Inference teaching path. The runnable simulator uses explicitly disclosed tiny, untrained weights.

nodes.title: Discard rejected suffix
nodes.subtitle: Rollback tentative KV positions
nodes.description: Discard the first mismatching proposal and every later proposal. Trim tentative main-model K/V positions to the accepted prefix. The correction is the main model token at the first mismatch.
notes: Inference teaching path. The runnable simulator uses explicitly disclosed tiny, untrained weights.

nodes.title: Commit verified tokens
nodes.subtitle: Accepted prefix + correction / bonus
nodes.description: Commit the accepted prefix and, when there is room in the token budget, a main-model correction at a mismatch or a bonus token if every proposal matched. No rejected proposal is appended to the confirmed sequence.
notes: Inference teaching path. The runnable simulator uses explicitly disclosed tiny, untrained weights.

nodes.title: Decode confirmed text
nodes.subtitle: Token IDs → UTF-8 bytes → text
nodes.description: Decode confirmed IDs through the same tokenizer vocabulary. Token IDs are appended as IDs for subsequent computation; generated text is not re-tokenized.
notes: Inference teaching path. The runnable simulator uses explicitly disclosed tiny, untrained weights.

nodes.title: Feed the next iteration
nodes.subtitle: Reuse committed KV state
nodes.description: Continue from the confirmed token sequence and main-model state. Stop at the requested output-token budget or the teaching context limit.
notes: Inference teaching path. The runnable simulator uses explicitly disclosed tiny, untrained weights.
